support: I laid my hand on her iron side and thought of the mornings, years ago, when I rode up behind her with her smoke drifting back past the carriage windows and the whole village hearing her whistle at Gessen.
The shed was quiet, and the smell of coal had long since gone from it.
WV13-P01.6.note: The author describes the working line neutrally and closes in longing for the steam-hauled climb that is gone; the 'builders cut into the mountainside' detail is factual rather than praise, so admiring is weaker than wistful, though it is the nearest rival.

support: When I stand at the deep end now, I still look up for a tower that is gone.
Three generations of Ostley children learned to dive from that tower, and the place where they learned has gone with it.
WV13-P02.5.note: The writer blames no one (the tower was unsound, the tiles split) but mourns the lost tower and tiles, which is regret rather than disapproval.
